headline: A technical law that fixes rules for federal job training programs and adjusts terms for the National Council on Disability.
what_it_does: The law changes the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, which funds job training and employment services. It revises rules for local workforce areas and local workforce boards, and it lets governors approve certain rural areas served by rural concentrated employment programs. It also sets a minimum funding level of 90% of the prior year's amount for adult, dislocated worker, and statewide workforce activities, and it changes the terms of service for National Council on Disability members.

who_it_affects.how: They must follow the revised rules for designating local workforce areas and may approve rural concentrated employment program areas for designation.
Their membership and eligibility rules are revised, including which existing local entities can serve as an alternative board.

who_it_affects.group: Adults, dislocated workers, and youth in job training programs
who_it_affects.how: The changes to performance accountability rules and funding allotments affect the programs that serve them.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the National Council on Disability
who_it_affects.how: Their terms of service requirements are revised and made effective as of July 21, 2014.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on May 22, 2015. The National Council on Disability term changes apply as of July 21, 2014.
